model.name: Test Case / Test Result
model.purpose: Provide a governed, format-neutral structure for repeatable software and system test cases together with the executions, results and evidence they produce, so an agent can define a reusable test, resolve it for execution, record what happened, adjudicate a governed verdict, retain defensible evidence, and expose that evidence to assurance and release consumers.
model.scope_statement: WM-SFT-015 models a versioned test-evidence aggregate. The reusable test case definition is the aggregate root: authoritative identity and revision, title and objective, classification, requirement, risk and acceptance-criterion traceability, preconditions, fixture and test-data references, inputs and parameters, ordered actions, expected outcomes, oracle and comparison rule with tolerances, postconditions, automation binding, applicability, dependencies, variants, ownership and readiness. Governed members are the executions of a specific frozen definition revision, their observed outcomes, adjudicated verdicts and result status, the evidence captured during execution, the assurance signals derived over that evidence, and the governance record of ownership, approval, access and retention that binds them. Test suites and test sets, test plans and campaigns, requirements and acceptance criteria, risks, builds and releases, defects and test environments are typed external references: the model carries the reference, the binding and subject-specific parameters, and never reproduces those neighbours' lifecycles or operational functions.
in_scope: Authoritative identity and revision history of a reusable test case, including the immutable definition snapshot that any execution cites.
Test intent: title, objective, test level and test type classification, and the design technique and coverage items from which a case is derived.
Typed traceability bindings from a test case revision to requirement, acceptance-criterion, risk, specification-statement and test-assertion references held by external models.
Preconditions and required entry state, expressed so they can be checked rather than assumed.
Fixture and test-data references with version, provisioning contract and sensitivity classification.
Declared inputs, parameters, value constraints and parameterized variants, including combinatorial or boundary-derived value sets.
Ordered actions and step structure, including delegation to reusable keywords or shared step definitions.
Expected outcomes, the oracle and comparison rule, tolerances, units and normalization rules, and postconditions with cleanup obligations.
Automation binding that names the executable implementation or keyword decomposition realising a test case revision.
Applicability conditions, selection tags and attributes, priority, and declared inter-case dependencies.
Governed execution records stating which definition revision was run, when, against which referenced test item and environment, by which actor and with which resolved parameters.
Observed outcomes, adjudicated verdicts, result status and reason codes, including reruns, retries and quarantined or unreliable results.
Evidence captured by an execution such as logs, measurements, screenshots, baselines and attachments, with provenance and integrity.
Assurance signals derived over the aggregate: traceability completeness, coverage claims, result reliability and readiness statements consumed by release assurance.
Governance of the aggregate: ownership and stewardship, review and approval state, access classification, and retention and disposition of test records.
out_of_scope: Test suite and test set membership, ordering and suite-level lifecycle.
Test plan, campaign and cycle scheduling, resourcing and exit-criteria management.
Requirement, user story, acceptance-criterion and risk authoring, approval and change lifecycle.
Build, release and deployment identity and release-gating decisions, which WM-SFT-008 owns.
Defect and incident triage, assignment and resolution lifecycle.
Test environment provisioning, configuration baselining and infrastructure state.
Source code and executable test script implementation together with its repository lifecycle.
Pipeline orchestration, runner scheduling and job dispatch mechanics.
Runtime policy evaluation, enforcement engines and organisation-wide audit-trail semantics owned by referenced governance models.
Test tool and framework product lifecycle, licensing and vendor management.
Lawfulness assessment and erasure execution for production-derived personal data used as test data, which the adopting Dimension's privacy and storage models own.

boundary_notes.distinction: A test case states what is verified, under which entry state, with which expected outcome. A test procedure sequences one or more test cases with set-up and wrap-up for a specific execution occasion and carries its own identity and lifecycle; this model references a procedure but does not own its ordering or approval.

The script is an artifact of a source repository with its own versioning, review and build lifecycle. This model holds only a resolvable binding reference plus the contract the implementation must satisfy, so implementation change does not fork the definition.

A suite is a grouping and ordering construct over cases. Membership, ordering and suite-level status live with the suite model; this model declares only the tags, attributes and traceability that make a case selectable.

Planning covers scope, schedule, resourcing, entry and exit criteria for an effort. This model supplies definitions and evidence that a plan consumes and never holds schedule, staffing or exit-criteria decisions.

A scenario describes intended usage for stakeholders and may be executable prose. A test case adds a verdict-bearing expectation with an oracle and comparison rule; an executable scenario is treated as one authoring form of a test case specification, not as a separate lifecycle.

Normative statements and the testable assertions derived from them sit in the test basis. One assertion may require several test cases and coverage is often imperfect, so traceability is a many-to-many typed reference, not ownership of the requirement lifecycle.
A defect is a reported anomaly with independent triage, assignment and closure. A failing result may cite a defect reference, but defect state never becomes result state inside this model.

Release assurance references test evidence held here. Release identity, release lifecycle, gating decisions and the release audit trail remain with WM-SFT-008; this model publishes resolvable evidence references only.
Environment identity, configuration baseline and provisioning are external. An execution record cites the environment reference so results stay interpretable, without importing environment lifecycle.

Master data sets have their own stewardship, versioning and privacy controls. This model references a data-set identifier and version and classifies sensitivity for the binding, but does not own generation, masking or erasure execution.

sources.title: IEEE/ISO/IEC International Standard for Software and systems engineering--Software testing--Part 3: Test documentation
sources.relevance: Official catalogue record for the test documentation standard providing templates and examples organised by the 29119-2 test processes; establishes that test case, test procedure, plan and incident documentation are distinct, tailorable document types supporting manual, automated, scripted and unscripted testing. Used at scope level, not clause level.

sources.title: IEEE/ISO/IEC International Standard - Software and systems engineering--Software testing--Part 4: Test techniques
sources.relevance: Official catalogue record for test design techniques used within test design and implementation; states that techniques derive test cases which when executed generate evidence that requirements are met or defects are present, and that risk-based testing determines applicable techniques. Grounds derivation and coverage-item structure.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE International Standard Software and systems engineering -- Software testing -- Part 5: Keyword-Driven Testing
sources.relevance: Defines keyword-driven testing as an approach to describing test cases in a modular way, sets framework and tool requirements, and defines a common data exchange format so tools can exchange test cases, test data and test results. Grounds automation binding, keyword decomposition and interchange.

sources.title: ISO/IEC/IEEE International Standard - Software and systems engineering -- Software testing -- Part 1: General concepts
sources.relevance: Official catalogue record establishing the concepts and vocabulary on which the 29119 series is built; used to justify treating test case, test procedure, suite and plan as distinct concepts rather than one artifact.

sources.title: Test Metadata
sources.relevance: Clause-level enumeration of test metadata: Identifier, Title, Purpose, Description, Status, SpecRef, Preconditions, Inputs, ExpectedResults, Version, Contributor, Rights, Grouping and SeeAlso, with required and optional marking. Primary evidence for identity, revision, objective, traceability, preconditions, inputs, expected results, ownership, rights and grouping.

sources.title: Test Assertions Model Version 1.0
sources.relevance: Defines identifier, normative source, target, prerequisite, predicate, prescription level, variable, tag and description, plus test assertion sets and implicit parts. States that one assertion may require several test cases and that test cases are indicators rather than proofs. Primary evidence for oracle predicates, prescription level, prerequisites, parameter variables and many-to-many traceability.

sources.title: ITU-T Recommendation Z.161: Testing and Test Control Notation version 3: TTCN-3 core language
sources.relevance: Standardised notation in which test cases are parameterized, reusable, declarative units with templates and matching mechanisms for expected values and an explicit verdict concept. Supports parameterization, template-based expected values, and the separation between declaring a comparison rule and resolving a verdict.

sources.title: NIST Special Publication 800-142, Practical Combinatorial Testing
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), U.S. Department of Commerce
sources.relevance: Public-authority guidance on input parameter modelling, t-way interaction coverage, constraints among parameter values, generated test sets, and the use of formal models to determine expected results for each set of inputs. Grounds parameter value selection, exclusion constraints and generator provenance.

sources.title: General Principles of Software Validation: Final Guidance for Industry and FDA Staff
sources.organization: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (CDRH and CBER)
sources.relevance: Regulated-context authority establishing that software validation rests on documented, requirement-traceable testing with predefined expected results and retained records. Used only as a regulated-context alignment for evidence retention and pre-declared expectations; clause text was not machine-readable in this research.

sources.title: Gherkin Reference
sources.relevance: First-party specification of an executable test case authoring form: Feature, Rule, Scenario, Given/When/Then steps, Background for shared set-up, Scenario Outline run once per Examples row for parameterized variants, data tables and doc strings for complex inputs, and tags for grouping independent of file structure.

sources.title: JUnit User Guide
sources.relevance: First-party evidence from a mature automation ecosystem for unique identifiers and display names, tags with tag expressions for selection and filtering, parameterized tests with argument sources for data-driven variants, assumptions for conditional applicability, disabling, test ordering, test templates, and the TestPlan and TestDescriptor separation between describing tests and executing them.

bundles.name: Test Case Identity and Intent
bundles.description: Everything needed to name a reusable test case unambiguously, to pin the exact revision an execution used, to state what the case exists to verify, and to bind it to the normative basis it was derived from.
bundles.rationale: Cited metadata and assertion specifications make an unambiguous identifier, a version, a stated purpose and a reference to the specification statements under test mandatory or near-mandatory properties of a test; without them a recorded result cannot be attributed to a definition and derivation from a test basis cannot be assessed. Technique and general-concept standards add the derivation chain from test basis through coverage items to cases.

layers.name: Identity and Revision Control
layers.description: The authoritative identifier of a test case, the identity of each revision of its definition, and the immutability guarantees that let past evidence stay interpretable.

findings.name: Authoritative test case identity
findings.description: How a reusable test case is uniquely and stably identified across authoring tools, repositories, management systems and execution systems, and how that identity survives renaming, relocation and tool migration. Identity is the anchor for every later reference from executions, evidence and release assurance.

questions.text: Which system holds the authoritative identifier for this test case, and what identifier value does it issue?
answer_data: Master-system reference for test case identity

questions.text: Which alternate or legacy identifiers must resolve to this test case, and in which external systems do they live?
answer_data: Issuing system reference per alternate identifier

questions.text: What identity guarantees hold when the test case is renamed, moved between repositories or migrated between tools?
What distinguishes one test case from a variant, a duplicate and a differently-named copy of the same test?
answer_data: Identity criteria set covering objective, oracle and parameter signature

data_elements.name: Test case identifier
data_elements.description: Authoritative identifier of the reusable test case, issued by the master system for test cases.

data_elements.name: Identifier scheme
data_elements.description: Coded scheme or namespace under which the authoritative identifier is unique.

data_elements.name: Master system reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the system of record that issued and governs the authoritative identifier.

data_elements.name: Alternate identifiers
data_elements.description: Legacy or external identifiers that must resolve to this test case, each with its issuing system.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identity here is pure reference data: an identifier value, its issuing scheme, the master-system pointer and alternate-identifier mappings are resolved inline by every consumer. Materialising identity as a separate stored artifact would create a second competing source of truth for the same identifier and would invite drift between that artifact and the master system.

findings.name: Revision identity and definition immutability
findings.description: How successive revisions of a test case definition are identified, superseded and frozen, so that any execution can name exactly the definition text it ran and a consumer can later prove the cited definition was not altered. Includes authorship and change-reason provenance of each revision.

questions.text: How is a new revision of the test case definition created, numbered and superseded?
Who authored or changed this revision, on what authority, and from which prior revision was it derived?
Which timestamps distinguish when a revision became effective from when the register recorded it?
answer_data: Effective event time in RFC 3339 with explicit offset
Recording or ingestion time in RFC 3339 with explicit offset

questions.text: Which changes to a definition require a new revision rather than an in-place editorial correction?
How can a consumer prove that the definition referenced by a past execution has not been altered?

data_elements.name: Revision identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of one revision of the test case definition, unique within the test case.

data_elements.name: Supersedes revision
data_elements.description: Reference to the revision that this revision replaces.

data_elements.name: Revision effective time
data_elements.description: Event time at which the revision became the effective definition.

data_elements.name: Revision recorded time
data_elements.description: Observation or ingestion time at which the model recorded the revision.

data_elements.name: Revision content digest
data_elements.description: Digest algorithm and value computed over the canonical serialization of the revision.

data_elements.name: Change reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason for creating the revision, drawn from a controlled vocabulary.

artifacts.name: Test case definition snapshot
artifacts.description: Immutable, canonically serialized capture of exactly one test case definition revision, addressable by content digest, cited by executions and evidence consumers to prove which definition text was in force.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identity is the content digest over the canonical serialization, bound to the authoritative test case identifier plus the revision identifier; the revision identifier gives the ordinal position in the series and the digest gives integrity. No date component participates in the identity.

layers.name: Objective, Classification and Test Basis Traceability
layers.description: What the test case exists to verify, how it is classified for selection and reporting, and the typed links and derivation record connecting it to requirements, acceptance criteria, risks and coverage items.

findings.name: Test objective, test item and classification
findings.description: The single stated purpose of the test case expressed independently of how it is executed, the test item or component under test, and the controlled classification of test level, test type and quality characteristic that drives selection and reporting.

questions.text: What single objective does this test case exist to verify, stated independently of how it is executed?
Which test level, test type and quality characteristic classify this test case, and from which controlled vocabulary?
Which test item, component or interface is under test, and how is it referenced?
How is the objective checked for being single-purpose, observable and falsifiable?

data_elements.name: Title
data_elements.description: Short human-readable name of the test case.

data_elements.name: Objective
data_elements.description: Statement of why the test exists and what it verifies.

data_elements.name: Test level
data_elements.description: Coded test level such as component, integration, system or acceptance.

data_elements.name: Test type
data_elements.description: Coded test type or quality characteristic addressed by the case.

data_elements.name: Test item reference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to the item, component or interface under test.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Objective, title, classification codes and the test item pointer are short structured values consumed at query time by selection, reporting and traceability functions. They have no rendering, media form or integrity requirement of their own, and any document that displays them is a projection of the definition snapshot already declared in this model.

findings.name: Test basis traceability and derivation record
findings.description: Typed links from a test case revision to the requirement, acceptance criterion, risk, specification statement or test assertion it was derived from, together with the design technique, coverage items and generation parameters that justify the derivation. Traceability is many-to-many by nature and does not claim one-to-one requirement coverage.

questions.text: Which requirement, acceptance-criterion, risk or specification statements does this test case revision trace to, and with what link type?
answer_data: Traceability link set with link type

questions.text: Which coverage items does this test case cover, and which test design technique produced them?
answer_data: Coverage model or test condition reference

questions.text: Which normative statement gives the expected outcome its authority, and what is its prescription level?
answer_data: Prescription level value such as mandatory, preferred or permitted

questions.text: How is traceability completeness assessed without asserting one-to-one coverage of a requirement?
Was the case written manually, derived from a model, or generated combinatorially, and with which generation parameters?
answer_data: Generation parameters such as interaction strength and constraints

data_elements.name: Traceability link
data_elements.description: Typed link from the test case revision to a test basis element held by an external model.

data_elements.name: Design technique
data_elements.description: Coded test design technique used to derive the case.

data_elements.name: Coverage item
data_elements.description: Identifier of a coverage item that this case is intended to cover.

data_elements.name: Prescription level
data_elements.description: Imperative force of the normative statement behind the expected outcome.

data_elements.name: Derivation method
data_elements.description: Coded method by which the case was produced, including generator provenance where applicable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Traceability is link data whose endpoints are owned by external requirement, acceptance-criterion and risk models. Storing a locally materialised traceability matrix would duplicate those models' content, would go stale on their change events, and would imply local ownership of requirement lifecycle that the reference boundary explicitly withholds; the links are therefore carried inline as typed references only.

bundles.name: Executable Test Specification
bundles.description: The verifiable substance of the test case: the entry state it needs, the fixtures and data it references, the stimulus it applies, the outcome it expects with the rule used to compare against it, and the end state it leaves behind.
bundles.rationale: Cited metadata and assertion specifications make preconditions, inputs, expected results and evaluable predicates first-class parts of a test; technique and combinatorial-testing guidance derives input values and expected results from coverage items and parameter models; and a standardised test notation expresses expected values as reusable, parameterized templates with explicit matching rules. This is the smallest coherent body of context that makes a case executable and its result adjudicable.

layers.name: Entry State, Fixtures and Test Data
layers.description: Conditions that must hold before execution begins and the versioned fixtures and data sets the case depends on, referenced rather than owned.

findings.name: Preconditions and required entry state
findings.description: The conditions that must hold before the case may be executed meaningfully, expressed so they can be checked rather than assumed, together with the disposition the definition declares when a precondition cannot be established. The definition declares intent; what actually happened in a given run is recorded by the execution structures of this model.

questions.text: What state must the test item, its data and the referenced environment be in before execution begins?
Which preconditions are mandatory gates and which are advisory assumptions that merely make the case inapplicable?
answer_data: Gate versus assumption flag per precondition

questions.text: How is each precondition established: by the case itself, by a referenced fixture, or by an external set-up step?
What disposition does the definition declare when a precondition cannot be established?
answer_data: Declared not-run or skip disposition code

data_elements.name: Precondition statement
data_elements.description: One checkable condition required before execution.

data_elements.name: Precondition kind
data_elements.description: Whether the precondition is a mandatory gate or an applicability assumption.

data_elements.name: Precondition check reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an executable or documented check that evaluates the precondition.

data_elements.name: Unmet precondition disposition
data_elements.description: Coded disposition the definition declares when a precondition cannot be established.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Preconditions are short declarative statements plus optional pointers to checks that live in fixtures or executable code owned elsewhere. They are read inline during authoring review and during resolution, and packaging them as a separate artifact would fragment one definition revision across two integrity anchors without adding any retrievable content.

findings.name: Fixture and test data references
findings.description: How the case names the fixtures, seed state and data sets it requires, with version, provisioning contract, determinism expectations and sensitivity classification, while the master lifecycle of that data stays with the owning test data system.

questions.text: Which fixtures and test data sets does this case require, and how are they referenced and versioned?
What sensitivity classification applies to the referenced test data, and is production-derived data permitted for this case?
Which parts of the referenced data are inputs, which are seeded state and which are expected baselines?
What determinism and isolation guarantees must the data satisfy for the expected outcome to hold?
How long must a referenced data set remain resolvable for past evidence to stay interpretable?
answer_data: Declared behaviour when a version is withdrawn

data_elements.name: Fixture reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a reusable fixture or shared background that establishes state for the case.

data_elements.name: Test data set reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of a referenced test data set.

data_elements.name: Data sensitivity class
data_elements.description: Classification of the referenced data governing access and masking.

data_elements.name: Provisioning mode
data_elements.description: How the data is made available: pre-seeded, generated at resolution, or supplied by the environment.

artifacts.name: Referenced test data set version
artifacts.description: A named, versioned collection of seed state and input values that a test case revision requires, held or referenced as a resolvable, integrity-checked object rather than re-authored per execution.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative data-set identifier issued by the owning test data system where one exists; otherwise a governed data-set IRI in a controlled namespace; otherwise a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Each version carries a content digest, and a test case reference names identifier plus version, never a file path or a date.

layers.name: Inputs, Parameters and Ordered Actions
layers.description: The declared parameter surface of the case, the value sets that produce data-driven variants, and the ordered actions that apply the stimulus.

findings.name: Inputs, parameters and parameterized variants
findings.description: Declared inputs and parameters with types, defaults and value constraints, the basis on which values or ranges are chosen, the exclusion of invalid combinations, and how a parameter set produces data-driven variants without fragmenting the identity of the parent case.

questions.text: Which parameters does the test case declare, with what types, defaults and value constraints?
When a parameter set produces many invocations, what is the identity of each variant relative to the parent test case?
answer_data: Declared decision on whether a variant is a distinct case

questions.text: On what sampling, boundary or interaction basis are the input values or ranges chosen?
Which parameter combinations are excluded as invalid, unreachable or unsafe?
How are parameter values bound at resolution time from external configuration or credential stores?
answer_data: Secret handling rule prohibiting stored secret values

data_elements.name: Parameter name
data_elements.description: Declared name of a test case parameter.

data_elements.name: Parameter type
data_elements.description: Declared type or value domain of a parameter.

data_elements.name: Parameter constraint
data_elements.description: Constraint restricting permitted values or combinations of values.

data_elements.name: Variant key
data_elements.description: Stable key identifying one parameter set of the parent test case.

data_elements.name: Parameter binding expression
data_elements.description: Expression resolving a parameter value from an external source at resolution time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Parameter declarations are structural metadata of the definition itself and belong inside the definition revision that is already snapshotted. The concrete value collections that fill them are held in the referenced test data set artifact declared in the fixture finding, so declaring a second artifact here would split one logical payload across two artifacts with competing versions.

findings.name: Ordered actions and step structure
findings.description: The ordered actions the test case prescribes, the granularity and identity of a step so expectations and evidence can attach to it, shared set-up versus discriminating actions, ordering significance, and delegation to reusable keywords or shared step definitions. The boundary against a test procedure that orders several cases is stated explicitly.

questions.text: What is the ordered sequence of actions the test case prescribes, and at what granularity is a step defined?
How is an individual step identified so that expected outcomes and captured evidence can attach to it?
answer_data: Stability rule when steps are inserted or removed

questions.text: Which steps are shared set-up or teardown and which are the discriminating actions of this case?
Is the step order significant, and which steps may be reordered, repeated or run concurrently?
Where a step delegates to a reusable keyword or shared step definition, how is that reference resolved?

data_elements.name: Step identifier
data_elements.description: Stable identifier of one action step within the test case revision.

data_elements.name: Step ordinal
data_elements.description: Position of the step in the prescribed order.

data_elements.name: Step action
data_elements.description: Statement of the action performed at this step.

data_elements.name: Step keyword reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a reusable keyword or shared step definition realising the step.

data_elements.name: Step concurrency permission
data_elements.description: Whether the step may run concurrently with adjacent steps.

artifacts.name: Test case specification document
artifacts.description: The authored, human- and machine-readable rendering of one test case revision covering objective, preconditions, ordered steps and expected outcomes, in the form in which authors maintain it, such as an executable scenario file, a keyword-driven step table or a structured specification document. Distinct from the definition snapshot, which is the canonical serialization used for integrity rather than for authoring.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the authoritative test case identifier plus the revision identifier; where the document is the authoring source of truth its repository object identifier is recorded, and its content digest must reconcile with the digest recorded on the corresponding definition snapshot.

layers.name: Expected Outcome, Oracle and End State
layers.description: What a conforming test item must produce, the rule and tolerance by which agreement is decided, the baselines the comparison uses, and the state the case must leave behind.

findings.name: Expected outcomes, oracle and tolerances
findings.description: What the case declares as correct behaviour per step and overall, the oracle and comparison rule used to decide agreement, tolerances and units for approximate comparisons, the baselines the comparison references, and the normalization or masking applied before comparison. The definition declares the comparison rule; adjudicating an actual observation against it and recording the resulting verdict are performed by the execution structures of this model.

questions.text: What outcome must a conforming test item produce, stated per step and for the case overall?
Which comparison rule, tolerance and units apply when the expected outcome is numeric or approximate?
Which reference baseline or golden artifact does the comparison use, and how is it versioned?
answer_data: Rule for approving a baseline update

questions.text: Which parts of an observed outcome are normalized, masked or ignored before comparison?
What agreement criterion does the definition fix, and what is explicitly left for result adjudication to decide?
answer_data: Handoff note to the adjudicating structures

data_elements.name: Expected outcome
data_elements.description: Statement of the outcome a conforming test item must produce, per step or overall.

data_elements.name: Comparison rule
data_elements.description: Predicate or matching rule that decides agreement between expected and observed outcome.

data_elements.name: Tolerance
data_elements.description: Permitted deviation for an approximate comparison.

data_elements.name: Tolerance unit
data_elements.description: Unit of measure in which the tolerance is expressed.

data_elements.name: Baseline reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the reference baseline used by the comparison.

data_elements.name: Normalization rule
data_elements.description: Rule normalizing, masking or ignoring parts of an observed outcome before comparison.

artifacts.name: Expected outcome baseline
artifacts.description: A versioned reference artifact holding the expected value, golden output, reference rendering or validation schema against which an observed outcome is compared.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative baseline identifier from the owning baseline store where one exists; otherwise a governed IRI; otherwise a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Every baseline version records a content digest and the test case revision that approved it, and sequence position rather than a date orders the series.

findings.name: Postconditions, end state and side-effect limits
findings.description: The state the case declares must hold after execution regardless of outcome, the cleanup or restoration obligations and who performs them, the state deliberately left for dependent cases, and the side effects that must never escape the test boundary.

questions.text: What state must hold after the case completes, independently of the outcome it produced?
answer_data: Required end state of the test item
Required end state of referenced data

questions.text: Which cleanup or restoration obligations does the case declare, and who performs them?
answer_data: Order relative to the final step

questions.text: Which downstream cases depend on state that this case deliberately leaves behind?
Which side effects are permitted, and which must never escape the test boundary?

data_elements.name: Postcondition statement
data_elements.description: Condition required to hold after the case completes.

data_elements.name: Cleanup obligation
data_elements.description: Declared restoration or teardown duty and its performing actor.

data_elements.name: Side-effect allowance
data_elements.description: Coded statement of permitted and prohibited side effects.

data_elements.name: Leaves residual state
data_elements.description: Whether the case intentionally leaves state for dependent cases.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Postconditions and side-effect limits are declarative constraints read during authoring review and during resolution; they produce no stored payload of their own. Any observed end state belongs to an execution record, which is a governed member of this aggregate rather than an artifact of the reusable definition.

bundles.name: Binding, Applicability and Readiness
bundles.description: What turns a reusable definition into something an agent may legitimately select and resolve: its binding to an executable implementation, the conditions and attributes that make it applicable and selectable, its dependencies, and the ownership and readiness state that authorises use.
bundles.rationale: Keyword-driven testing standards make the decomposition of a case into reusable keywords and its exchange between frameworks explicit; first-party automation ecosystems make unique identifiers, tags with selection expressions, parameterized variants and conditional applicability explicit; and cited metadata makes Status, Contributor and Rights required properties. A definition without binding, applicability and an accountable owner cannot be safely resolved for execution.

layers.name: Automation Binding, Applicability and Dependencies
layers.description: How a definition points at the implementation that realises it, and the declared conditions, attributes and dependencies that determine when it is applicable and selectable.

findings.name: Automation binding to an executable implementation
findings.description: How a test case revision names the executable implementation, keyword decomposition or generated harness that realises it, the framework contract that binding must satisfy, how broken or ambiguous bindings are detected, and the automation status of the case. The implementation's own repository lifecycle stays outside this model.

questions.text: Which executable implementation realises this test case revision, and how is it addressed?
answer_data: Implementation reference such as repository, path and symbol

questions.text: Which automation framework contract must the implementation satisfy for the binding to be valid?
How is a binding detected as broken, ambiguous or pointing at a different revision than intended?
Is this case manual, automatable, automated or generated, and who decides that status?
What must remain true of the definition when only the implementation changes?
answer_data: Revision impact rule for implementation-only change

data_elements.name: Automation status
data_elements.description: Coded status describing whether and how the case is automated.

data_elements.name: Implementation reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the executable implementation realising the case.

data_elements.name: Framework identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the automation framework or engine that the binding targets.

data_elements.name: Binding resolution rule
data_elements.description: Rule by which an implementation reference is resolved at resolution time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The executable script is an artifact of the source repository that owns its review, build and release lifecycle. Declaring it as an artifact of this model would fork that lifecycle and place implementation change control inside a model whose boundary explicitly withholds it, so only a resolvable binding reference and its validity contract are carried inline.

findings.name: Applicability, selection attributes and dependencies
findings.description: The conditions under which a case is applicable, the tags, attributes and priority used to select it into a scope, time-bounded applicability, and declared dependencies on other cases. Evaluating a selection expression to build and dispatch an actual run belongs to the referenced suite, campaign and pipeline models.

questions.text: Which tags, attributes and priority values are declared for selection, and from which vocabulary?
Under which product configurations, platforms, locales or feature flags is this case applicable?
Which other test cases must have succeeded, or must not run concurrently, for this case to be meaningful?
What selection expression would an agent evaluate to include this case in a given scope, and which model owns evaluating and scheduling it?
answer_data: Statement that evaluation, sequencing and dispatch are owned by referenced suite, campaign and pipeline models

questions.text: Is applicability time-bounded, for example pending a fix, a deprecation date or a seasonal window?
answer_data: Applicable-from time in RFC 3339 with explicit offset
Applicable-until time in RFC 3339 with explicit offset

data_elements.name: Selection tag
data_elements.description: Tag value declared on the case for grouping and selection.

data_elements.name: Priority
data_elements.description: Coded priority or importance used during selection.

data_elements.name: Applicability condition
data_elements.description: Condition restricting the configurations, platforms or locales where the case applies.

data_elements.name: Depends-on case reference
data_elements.description: Reference to another test case whose outcome or residual state this case depends on.

data_elements.name: Applicable from
data_elements.description: Event time from which the case is applicable.

data_elements.name: Applicable until
data_elements.description: Event time after which the case ceases to be applicable.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Applicability conditions, tags, priority and dependency pointers are queryable attributes of the definition consumed by selection at request time. Persisting them as a stored artifact would snapshot a selection surface that changes with each revision, and any materialised candidate list belongs to the referenced suite or campaign model rather than here.

layers.name: Stewardship and Readiness
layers.description: Who is accountable for a definition, how it is reviewed, who may read or change it, and the readiness state that declares a revision fit to be resolved for execution.

findings.name: Ownership, review and readiness for execution
findings.description: The accountable owner and day-to-day maintainer of the definition, the review criteria and approval authority, the permitted readiness states and transitions of a definition revision, and the access distinctions that apply to reading and changing it. This concerns the definition's own readiness, not the state of any execution.

questions.text: Which role or team owns this test case definition, and who maintains it day to day?
Which readiness states can a definition revision hold, and which transitions between them are permitted?
Who may approve a revision as ready for execution, and on what basis?
Who may read, propose changes to and publish this definition, and which parts are restricted?
answer_data: Read, propose and publish role assignments

data_elements.description: Reference to the accountable owner of the test case definition.

data_elements.name: Maintainer reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party maintaining the definition day to day.

data_elements.name: Readiness state
data_elements.description: Coded state of the definition revision such as draft, in review, ready, deprecated or retired.

data_elements.name: Approver reference

findings.inline_only_rationale: Readiness is a small inline state field with role references and review outcomes. The durable approval record and its audit trail are held by this model's governance structures and by the adopting Dimension's approval and audit systems, so declaring a separate design-side artifact here would create a competing copy of a record this layer does not own.

functions.name: Define a reusable test case
functions.description: Author a new test case definition from a stated objective and test basis references, capturing preconditions, fixture and data references, parameters, ordered actions, expected outcomes with a comparison rule, postconditions, applicability and ownership.
inputs: Test basis references covering requirement, acceptance criterion, risk and assertion
Preconditions and fixture or data-set references
Expected outcomes, comparison rule and tolerances
outputs: Assigned authoritative identifier or identifier request
Recorded authorship with event time and observation time
preconditions: Declared test basis references resolve in their owning models
The requesting actor holds an authoring role in the owning package
effects: Creates a draft definition revision in the register with event time and recording time
Registers typed references to external models without copying their content
Creates no execution record and adjudicates no result

functions.name: Version and freeze a test case revision
functions.description: Create the next revision of a definition when a semantic change occurs, freeze the superseded revision, and publish the canonical snapshot and digest that executions and evidence will cite.
outputs: Supersession link to the prior revision
preconditions: The change is classified as semantic under the materiality rule
Canonicalization rules are available for the target projection
effects: Freezes the superseded revision so past citations stay valid
Publishes an immutable definition snapshot addressable by digest
Leaves already-recorded executions pointing at the revision they actually used

functions.name: Validate a test case definition
functions.description: Statically assess one definition revision for completeness, internal consistency and traceability sufficiency against a declared validation profile, and report findings to authors and reviewers.
inputs: Validation profile naming required fields and rules
Controlled vocabularies for classification and status
preconditions: The validation profile declares which fields are required in this Dimension
effects: Records static validation findings against the definition revision
Blocks the readiness transition while a mandatory finding is open
Does not exercise the test item and produces no test verdict

functions.name: Select candidate test case revisions
functions.description: Return the set of test case revisions matching a selection expression over declared tags, attributes, traceability links and applicability context at a stated point in time, with the reason each case was included or excluded.
inputs: Selection expression over tags, attributes and traceability
Applicability context such as platform, configuration, locale and feature flags
Point in time for time-bounded applicability
outputs: Candidate set of test case revisions
Inclusion and exclusion reasons per case
preconditions: Selectable attributes are populated on the candidate definitions
The selection expression parses against the declared grammar
effects: Returns a candidate set as a read-only result
Leaves sequencing into suites, scheduling and dispatch to the referenced suite, campaign and pipeline models
Creates no execution record and changes no definition state

functions.name: Resolve a definition for execution
functions.description: Bind one test case revision, one parameter set, the referenced fixture and data-set versions and the automation binding into a fully-resolved definition handle that the execution structures cite when they record what was run.
inputs: Automation binding context and framework identifier
outputs: Resolved definition handle carrying resolved parameters, data-set versions, implementation reference, comparison rule and tolerances
Resolution report listing every reference that was resolved
Unresolvable reference list where resolution failed
preconditions: The revision is in a readiness state permitted for execution
All required bindings and data-set versions resolve
Excluded parameter combinations are not requested
effects: Emits an immutable resolved-definition handle bound to the revision digest
Hands that handle to the execution structures, which own running the test and recording and adjudicating its result
Performs no execution itself and adjudicates no verdict itself

composition.purpose: Positions the test-evidence aggregate beneath its registered parent so generic activity framing is inherited rather than restated; this model contributes only test-specific definition, execution, evidence, assurance and governance semantics.

Release assurance references test case revisions, executions and evidence held here. This model publishes stable, resolvable evidence references and carries no release identity, no release lifecycle, no release-gating decision and no release audit trail.
Carries typed traceability links and the prescription level of the normative statement behind an expected outcome, while requirement authoring, approval and change lifecycle remain with the target.
Carries risk references that justify technique choice and priority for a case; risk identification, assessment and treatment lifecycle remain with the target.

composition.target: Test suite / test set and test campaign model
composition.purpose: Supplies selectable definitions and evidence to suites and campaigns; membership, ordering, scheduling, resourcing and exit criteria remain with the target.
Execution records cite an environment reference so results stay interpretable; provisioning, configuration baselining and infrastructure state remain with the target.
A failing result may cite a defect reference; defect triage, assignment, resolution and closure remain with the target and never become result state here.
Names data-set identifiers, versions and sensitivity classification required by a case; data generation, masking, stewardship and erasure execution remain with the target.

Aligns field naming and document boundaries with an international test documentation standard without claiming conformance; recorded as an alignment because clause-level template content was not verified in this research.
Aligns identity, title, purpose, status, specification reference, preconditions, inputs, expected results, version, contributor, rights and grouping to a published metadata vocabulary for tests.

Aligns normative source, prerequisite, predicate, prescription level, variable and tag to the traceability, precondition, oracle and parameter structures here, and adopts its many-to-many relation between normative statements and test cases.
Aligns keyword decomposition and the interchange of test cases, test data and results with a standardised exchange format so definitions remain portable between frameworks.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension names one accountable owner package for test case definitions and revisions and one for execution, result and evidence records, both bound to the same model version.
The owner package declares the authoritative master system for test case identifiers and the fallback identifier scheme used where no master system exists.
The owner package declares controlled vocabularies for test level, test type, automation status, readiness state, change reason and result status codes.
The owner package declares the retention class for definitions and evidence and names the privacy model that governs referenced test data.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use one namespace per owning product or service, for example <dimension>/sft/test-case/<product>. Test case identifiers are unique within the namespace and never encode dates, folder paths, tool names or outcomes; revision identifiers are ordinals within the case rather than timestamps.
registry_links: Registry entry vr.wm-sft-015 at nav path NAV.INF.SFT.TST
Consumer model WM-SFT-008, where a build or release references test evidence

canonicalization_rules: Serialize a definition revision with sorted keys, UTF-8 text in NFC, absent fields omitted rather than null-valued, and RFC 3339 timestamps, then digest the result; that digest is the revision's integrity anchor.
Normalize every outbound reference to identifier plus version; never canonicalize a display name, file path or tool URL as identity.
Trim insignificant leading and trailing whitespace in step text while preserving significant whitespace inside doc strings and data tables.
patch_rules: Editorial patches to wording, formatting or description may update a revision in place with recorded editor, reason and observation time; semantic patches to preconditions, parameters, actions, expected outcomes, comparison rule, tolerances, postconditions or bindings require a new revision.
Patches are expressed as field-scoped operations carrying before and after values and a change reason code; a patch never rewrites a superseded revision or a published snapshot.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional declaration is backward compatible; removing or narrowing a declared parameter, tolerance, expected outcome or binding contract is breaking and requires a new major revision.
Consumers must tolerate unknown optional fields, must not infer meaning from field order, and must fail loudly rather than silently substitute when a referenced version cannot be resolved.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for test cases in the adopting Dimension
Governed global identifier or IRI from a controlled namespace where no master-system identifier exists
UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with its assigning authority
Content digest of the canonical serialization, used only as an integrity anchor and never as the primary business identity
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or Z. Event time, meaning when an authoring change, approval, applicability bound or execution actually occurred, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning when this model recorded it; where the two differ both are stored, and elapsed values use ISO 8601 duration form rather than a bare number.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely definition snapshots, test data set versions and expected baselines, are named <case-identifier>/<revision-identifier>/<artifact-role>/<sequence>, where sequence is a zero-padded monotonic integer; a date, a tool name or an outcome is never used as the sequence.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every stored artifact records digest algorithm and value, byte size, media type and the revision it belongs to. A reference whose recorded digest cannot be reproduced is reported as unresolvable and the dependent evidence is marked uninterpretable rather than silently substituted with a newer version.

policies: A definition revision that has been resolved for execution is immutable; corrections create a new revision so recorded evidence remains interpretable against the text that was actually run.
Expected outcomes and comparison rules are declared before execution; a definition is never edited to match an observed outcome.
Production-derived personal data may be referenced as test data only under the adopting Dimension's privacy model, and concrete sensitive values are never inlined into a definition or a snapshot.
External standards are treated as alignments; conformance is claimed only where cited evidence of an assessment exists, and the evidence tier of each citation is recorded.

read: Resolve a test case by authoritative identifier with an optional revision, defaulting to the latest revision in a readiness state permitted for execution.
Read a frozen revision snapshot by content digest in order to interpret historical evidence.
Query definitions by tags, attributes, traceability links, applicability context and readiness state, returning inclusion and exclusion reasons.
create: Create a draft definition revision recording author, creation event time and observation time.
Register alternate identifiers and typed references to external requirement, risk, suite, environment and data-set models.
Register a referenced test data set version or expected baseline version together with its digest and sensitivity classification.
update: Apply editorial updates in place with recorded editor and reason; apply semantic updates only by creating a new revision.
Transition readiness state through permitted transitions with approver reference, transition event time and observation time.
Re-point a broken or ambiguous automation binding, retaining the previous binding value and the reason for the change.
delete: Test case definitions and their revisions are never hard-deleted while any execution or evidence record cites them: they are withdrawn or retired and retained under the declared retention class, leaving a tombstone that keeps identifier, revision identifier, digest, withdrawal reason and effective time resolvable.

Records with no citing evidence may be disposed after the retention period declared by the adopting Dimension's records-retention policy; where a sector or jurisdiction imposes a longer retention duty on validation evidence, that duty overrides the local default.

Physical erasure of referenced test data containing personal data is executed by the adopting Dimension's privacy and storage models, not by this model; this model records the erasure request reference and marks the data-set reference as redacted while preserving the surrounding evidence chain.

Deletion of build, release, defect, suite, campaign and environment records is owned by those referenced models; this model removes only its own outbound reference and records the reason and time of removal.

roles.name: Test case author
responsibilities: Draft and maintain definitions including objective, preconditions, parameters, actions and postconditions
Declare traceability links, comparison rules and tolerances
Respond to validation findings before requesting review

roles.name: Test case reviewer and approver
responsibilities: Assess review criteria including objective atomicity and oracle soundness
Approve or reject a revision's transition to a readiness state permitted for execution
Record the approval basis and the reason for any rejection

roles.name: Test data steward
responsibilities: Register and version referenced data sets and expected baselines with digests
Classify data sensitivity and enforce the prohibition on inlining sensitive values
Confirm resolvability of referenced versions for the declared retention period

roles.name: Automation engineer
responsibilities: Maintain bindings between definition revisions and executable implementations
Declare and verify the framework contract a binding must satisfy
Report and repair broken or ambiguous bindings without altering definition semantics

roles.name: Model steward and registrar
responsibilities: Govern identifiers, namespaces, controlled vocabularies and revision materiality rules
Maintain alignment records and record conflicts with external standards
Adjudicate boundary questions against the composition and reference contract

roles.name: Evidence consumer
responsibilities: Resolve frozen revisions and evidence references read-only for assurance and release purposes
Refrain from creating or modifying definitions

access.default_rule: Read access to test case definitions is granted to delivery and assurance roles of the owning product package; write access is limited to authors, approvers and stewards of that package; anonymous access and cross-Dimension access are denied unless explicitly granted.
exceptions: Findings and artifacts containing security test payloads, credential material or exploit detail are restricted to a named security role and excluded from general reads.
Artifacts referencing personal or production-derived data inherit the sensitivity classification of the referenced data set and are masked or withheld in general reads.
Regulated evidence consumers such as auditors or notified bodies may be granted time-boxed read access to frozen revisions, snapshots and evidence references, recorded with the granting authority.
A broken-glass read of a restricted artifact may be granted for incident investigation, subject to after-the-fact review by the model steward.
audit_requirements: Record who read a restricted artifact and when, using event time and observation time in RFC 3339.
Record every readiness-state transition and binding change with actor, reason and both time values.
Store access decisions in the adopting Dimension's audit system and retain only the reference to that record here; this model does not own audit-trail semantics or their retention.

required_fields: Retention class and privacy model reference
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL.
Read the specification to learn the bundles, layers, findings and required data elements before writing anything.
Read the storage type description to learn projection, canonicalization and digest rules for the deployed store, including MongoDB or MCP deployments.
Read the interface description before issuing any read or write call.
Read the processes description before defining, versioning, validating, selecting or resolving a test case, and before citing a revision from an execution or evidence record.

coverage.claim: This research grounds a versioned test-evidence aggregate in catalogue-level ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 records together with clause-level W3C, OASIS and ITU-T specifications, NIST and FDA public-authority guidance, and first-party documentation from two mature testing ecosystems. The definition surface of the aggregate, covering identity, revision and immutability, objective and classification, test basis traceability and derivation, preconditions, fixtures and test data, inputs, parameters and variants, ordered actions, expected outcomes with oracle and tolerances, postconditions, automation binding, applicability and dependencies, ownership and readiness, is structured in detail and every node cites primary support. The functions inspected in this research task are the definition-side operations of defining, versioning, validating, selecting and resolving; by design they stop at handing a resolved, digest-bound definition to the model's execution structures, which own running the test and recording and adjudicating its governed result.

checklist.notes: Authoritative identifier, issuing scheme, master system, alternate identifiers, revision identity, step identity and variant identity are modelled, with identity priority fixed in artifact rules and no date-like component permitted in any identifier.

The definition's own lifecycle of draft, review, ready, deprecated and retired with permitted transitions and approval authority is modelled here; the execution and result lifecycle is in scope for the model and is carried by its execution structures rather than restated on the definition surface.

Traceability to requirements, acceptance criteria, risks and assertions, test item references, keyword and step-definition delegation, inter-case dependencies and twelve typed composition links are declared; every neighbour link is a reference that withholds the target's lifecycle.

Revision effective time versus recording time, time-bounded applicability and transition times are modelled; the timestamp rule fixes RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset and separates event time from observation or ingestion time.

Authorship, change reason, derived-from revision, derivation method with generator parameters, and contributor and rights fields are captured; digests bind a cited definition to the text that was in force.
Accountable owner, maintainer, approver, rights statement and six governance roles are declared, and owner-package requirements are fixed in the dimension service layer.

A static validation function with a declared profile, binding-integrity checks, traceability completeness assessment and review criteria are modelled; validation deliberately stops short of exercising the test item.

A deny-by-default rule, four access scopes, four exception classes including security payloads and personal data, and audit references are declared, with audit-trail ownership left to the adopting Dimension.

Withdrawal and tombstoning rather than hard deletion while evidence cites a revision, retention-class-driven disposition, regulated-duty override, delegated erasure of personal test data, and reference-only removal for neighbour records are all stated.

Alignments to W3C Test Metadata, the OASIS Test Assertions Model and the 29119-5 exchange format, framework binding contracts, alternate identifier mapping and parameter binding from external sources are declared as alignments rather than conformance claims.
Test level, test type, quality characteristic, automation status, priority, tags and data sensitivity class are declared against controlled vocabularies named by the owner package.
Comparison rule, tolerance value and unit, rounding and precision, normalization and masking, and combinatorial value selection with interaction strength are modelled.

Sensitivity classification of referenced data, prohibition on inlining sensitive values and secrets, masked reads and delegated erasure are modelled; lawfulness assessment stays with the adopting Dimension's privacy model.

Definition snapshots, data-set versions and expected baselines carry digest, byte size and media type, and a digest mismatch marks dependent evidence uninterpretable rather than resolving to a newer version.

No cited source fixes a normative threshold for when traceability or coverage is sufficient. The model records a coverage claim and uncovered coverage items but leaves the adequacy threshold to the adopting Dimension; this node is marked a gap rather than presented as canonical.
Platform, configuration and locale applicability conditions are modelled as constraints; localized authoring keywords are recorded as a parsing consideration under regional assumptions.

known_omissions: Clause-level text of ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 templates and 29119-4 technique definitions was not machine-readable in this research; catalogue scope and abstract text were used and no field-level structure rests on those citations alone.

The official ISTQB glossary is a client-rendered application that could not be retrieved, so ISTQB terminology is not used as normative evidence anywhere in this result despite being a preferred source class.
Non-functional test design parameters such as load profiles, performance workload models and security abuse cases are represented only generically through parameters, tolerances and classification.

Model-based testing artefacts such as behaviour models and generation grammars, and structural constructs of standardised test notations such as components, ports and defaults, are referenced but not modelled.
Accessibility and localisation-specific expected-outcome rules, and property-based or metamorphic oracle families, are not specialised beyond the generic comparison-rule structure.
Cost, effort and maintenance-burden attributes of a test case, which some management systems treat as first-class, are omitted for want of primary support.
conflicts: Common ecosystem usage treats a test script as the automated implementation while some standards usage treats it as a synonym for a test procedure; the model avoids the term entirely and uses ordered actions plus automation binding.

W3C Test Metadata makes Identifier, Purpose, SpecRef, ExpectedResults, Version, Contributor and Rights required, whereas ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119-3 documentation templates are explicitly tailorable; no universal mandatory field set can be claimed, so the required set is delegated to a validation profile.

The OASIS Test Assertions Model states that one assertion may require several test cases and that coverage is often imperfect, which contradicts any naive one-to-one requirement-to-test-case traceability assumption.

Parameterized constructs are treated as one case with many invocations by automation frameworks but frequently as distinct cases by test management systems; the model therefore requires variant identity to be declared rather than inferred.

Keyword-driven decomposition places ordered actions in a shared keyword library, so step content may be partly owned outside the case; the model records the delegation reference instead of copying keyword bodies.

Regulated validation guidance expects durable, requirement-traceable test records while fast-moving ecosystems routinely delete or rewrite tests; the immutability policy resolves this in favour of new revisions plus tombstones.
regional_assumptions: FDA General Principles of Software Validation is United States medical-device guidance; comparable duties elsewhere, including EU medical device regulation with IEC 62304, aerospace DO-178C, automotive ISO 26262 and rail EN 50128, impose analogous but differently worded documentation and retention obligations.
Retention periods for test evidence are jurisdiction- and sector-specific and are declared by the adopting Dimension rather than by this model.

Constraints on production-derived personal data used as test data assume a GDPR-like regime where one applies; other regimes permit or forbid different practices, and the privacy model reference absorbs the difference.

Authoring language and locale are assumed to be declared by the adopting Dimension; localized keywords in executable scenario formats affect parsing and must be recorded with the specification document.
adversarial_checks: The aggregate-root assumption was challenged directly. Exploratory and session-based testing produces results and evidence with no pre-existing reusable definition, and property-based or combinatorial generation produces runs whose definition is a generator plus a seed. Both are genuine counterexamples to a strict definition-root aggregate and are recorded for boundary adjudication rather than suppressed; the model accommodates them only by allowing a generator reference and generation parameters as derivation provenance.

Independent-lifecycle counterexamples were sought and found. A definition may be retired while its past executions remain under a legal retention duty, one execution may satisfy several test cases at scenario or session level, and one case may be realised by several independent implementations. The binding is therefore modelled as a citation of a frozen, digest-bound revision, which supports many-to-many relations without either side owning the other.

Every bundle, layer, finding and function was compared against the WM-SFT-008 reference rationale and against each outgoing reference and alignment. No local structure carries release-gating decisions, release lifecycle, suite membership or ordering, campaign scheduling, defect triage, environment provisioning, pipeline dispatch, runtime policy enforcement or organisation-wide audit-trail semantics; the selection function explicitly returns candidates and leaves sequencing and dispatch to the referenced models, and the access audit requirements store only a reference to the audit record.

Attractive but unsupported structure was rejected: a locally owned traceability matrix, a local coverage-adequacy threshold, a local flakiness-scoring algorithm, a local defect-linking workflow and a local copy of executable scripts were each considered and rejected for want of primary support or because they would fork a neighbour's lifecycle. Coverage adequacy is recorded as an explicit gap instead of being invented.

An evidence-tier check was applied to every citation. ISO/IEC/IEEE 29119 references are catalogue records carrying scope and abstract text rather than clause text and are labelled as such; every field-level structure is additionally supported by a clause-level source or a first-party ecosystem reference, and the two preferred source classes that could not be retrieved are listed as known omissions rather than paraphrased from secondary summaries.

A terminology counterexample search was run against a mature automation ecosystem that collapses case, procedure and script into a single annotated method, which would justify merging those concepts. The separation was retained because the cited standards distinguish them and because the reuse requirement of one definition, many executions and several possible bindings cannot be expressed once they are merged.
